channel.title: Ibrahim Alobaid — Articles
channel.description: A progressive engineering series on building natural, interruption-aware, production-ready voice AI agents — from digital audio and speech recognition to LLM conversation state.

item.title: The Voice Agent's Brain: LLMs and Conversation State
item.description: We now know how STT transcribes speech and how TTS speaks a reply. Between those stages sits the large language model (LLM). It interprets what the user wants and produces an appropriate response.

item.title: Text-to-Speech: How to Make a Voice Agent Sound Natural
item.description: In Article 03, we explored how a speech recognizer converts audio into text. Now we reverse that direction. How can an agent turn its answer into speech that is intelligible, natural, low latency…

item.title: Speech-to-Text: How Machines Turn Spoken Language into Text
item.description: In many voice-agent architectures, the first step toward “understanding speech” is actually Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR): mapping incoming audio to text. That transcript is not an infallible record.

item.title: Digital Audio for Developers: The Foundation of Every Voice AI Agent
item.description: Before your user's speech reaches a speech recognition model, it has already become numbers. Without a working understanding of sampling, sample rate, bit depth, PCM, channels, chunks, and codecs, you can misinterpret those numbers, feed a model the wrong audio format, or add avoidable latency.

item.title: What Is a Voice AI Agent? From Speech to Natural Conversation
item.description: A Voice AI Agent is not simply a speech recognition model, nor is it a synthetic voice reading an LLM's answer. It is an end-to-end interactive system that receives audio, interprets a user's intent, decides what to do next, responds through speech, and manages timing, context, and interruptions.
